h1: 24rooms Nakhon Sawan — a small stay with big, cute, spacious rooms in the heart of Pak Nam Pho
intro: If you want a place in the Pak Nam Pho town centre that is not just another identical hotel block, but a small homestay-style stay with spacious, cutely decorated rooms at a gentle price — 24rooms Nakhon Sawan is a new name worth watching. It is a budget stay opened in 2025 with only around 12 rooms, on Suanwitthi Road in the heart of town, within walking distance of the Walking Street and the Chao Phraya riverfront. The draw is the spacious rooms of about 36 sqm, the cleanliness, the friendly staff and free parking. Rooms start from about ฿750/night.

body.html: 24rooms Nakhon Sawan is a small stay that opened in 2025, on Suanwitthi Road in the Pak Nam Pho subdistrict, right in the heart of Nakhon Sawan. Unlike the usual chain budget hotels, this is a small homestay-style stay with only around 12 rooms, each decorated differently with a cute touch. The thing guests agree on most is that the rooms are larger than you would expect for the price, around 36 sqm, clean, with comfortable beds. The central location means you can walk or drive to the Walking Street, the Pak Nam Pho market and the Chao Phraya riverfront in no time — a good fit for anyone who wants to stay in town rather than out by the big road.

There are several room types, from a Standard up to a Deluxe and a Suite with a large bath. Inside you get air conditioning, a TV, a work desk, an en-suite bathroom and free toiletries, with some rooms looking onto a small garden. Real guest reviews praise the spacious, very clean rooms, the soft, comfortable beds and bedding, and the cute design that does not feel like a typical budget stay. Because it is small and newly opened, everything in the rooms still feels fresh and well looked after — the trade-off is that with so few rooms it fills up fast on holidays, so book ahead.

"The room was bigger than I expected, very clean, cutely decorated and the bed was comfortable. The staff were friendly and helpful, it is right in the town centre within walking distance of the Walking Street, and parking was easy."

Service is another point guests praise. Staff are praised for being friendly and helpful, the front desk is open 24 hours, check-in and check-out are quick, and they help with luggage and booking taxis. There is breakfast in the morning and a small restaurant/cafe corner. The free on-site parking is a genuine advantage for self-drivers. The limits are that, being a small stay, there is no swimming pool, gym or big-hotel facilities, and a small number of reviews mention a musty smell in some bathrooms that needs the ventilation fan kept on.

The Pak Nam Pho town-centre location suits people who want to explore in town. It is about 1 km to the Walking Street, near the Theparak-Thaptim Shrine and the Chao Phraya riverfront. The Nakhon Sawan observation tower (Sawan Park) and Bueng Boraphet are within easy driving distance for a side trip. Being central, there are plenty of noodle shops, morning eateries and cafes around. The overall score sits at around 8.4 from reviews on Trip.com — a solid result for a newly opened stay that does not yet have many reviews.

To be honest, 24rooms is not a hotel with a pool or full big-hotel facilities, and it does not yet have many accumulated reviews because it is new. The things to bear in mind are that it has very few rooms so it fills fast on long weekends and festivals, and a small number of reviews mention a musty bathroom smell. If you want a hotel with a pool and an in-house restaurant, Grand Hill Resort and Spa or Bonito Chinos Hotel may suit you better. But if you want a small stay with spacious, cutely decorated, clean rooms, free parking and a central location you can explore on foot, at a gentle price — this is a charming, good-value choice.

Tips from people who follow the reviews here: with only around 12 rooms, book several weeks ahead for holidays as the good rooms go fast. If you want a larger room with a bath, ask about the Suite when booking. Make the most of the central location — it is an easy evening stroll to the Walking Street and the Chao Phraya riverfront. The free on-site parking is an advantage for self-drivers, and always compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking, as small stays move their rates with the season.

faq.q: Where is 24rooms Nakhon Sawan and is it easy to reach?
faq.a: It sits at 60/89 Suanwitthi Road, Pak Nam Pho subdistrict, in the heart of Nakhon Sawan. It is about 1 km to the Pak Nam Pho Walking Street on foot or by car, near the Theparak-Thaptim Shrine and the Chao Phraya riverfront. The Nakhon Sawan observation tower is about 10 minutes by car and Bueng Boraphet about 15 minutes — the location suits people who want to stay in town and explore on foot.

faq.q: How much does 24rooms Nakhon Sawan cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from about ฿750/night for a Standard of around 36 sqm. There are also Deluxe rooms and a Suite with a large bath. During long weekends or festivals the rate climbs and rooms fill fast. Prices vary by date and platform, so always compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Who is 24rooms Nakhon Sawan best for?
faq.a: It is a great fit for anyone who wants a small stay with spacious, cutely decorated, clean rooms in a central, walkable location at a gentle price. It suits couples, solo travellers or small families who want to stay in the Pak Nam Pho town rather than a hotel out by the big road, and who do not mind there being no pool.

faq.q: What are the rooms at 24rooms Nakhon Sawan like?
faq.a: Spacious rooms of around 36 sqm, very clean, uniquely and cutely decorated, with comfortable beds are what guests agree on. They have air conditioning, a TV, a work desk and an en-suite bathroom. The trade-off is that it is a small, newly opened stay with no pool, and a small number of reviews mention a musty smell in some bathrooms.

There is free private parking, convenient for self-drivers, along with a 24-hour front desk and taxi booking. There is also breakfast served in the morning, around 8:00–10:00 AM, plus a small restaurant/cafe corner. As a small stay, there is no swimming pool or gym.

faq.q: 24rooms is newly opened — is it worth booking?
faq.a: It is a stay opened in 2025, so everything in the rooms still feels fresh and well looked after. The overall score sits at around 8.4 from Trip.com reviews, a solid result for a place that does not yet have many reviews. With only around 12 rooms, book several weeks ahead for holidays and choose free cancellation if your plans are not fixed.
